title: Transactional rollback planner for Terraform EKS control plane upgrades + health attestations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Ship a Terraform module and small orchestration shim that executes control-plane upgrades as a transactional sequence with an explicit rollback planner driven by health attestations. The module should make EKS control-plane upgrades (certificate/endpoint/stack changes and nodegroup rotations that touch control-plane reachability) safer in private VPC deployments by: 1) generating an immutable, versioned execution plan (plan ID + signatures) before any apply; 2) running a staged apply that emits health attestations at each orchestration step; 3) if a step fails health gates, create a deterministic rollback plan and mark the cluster for automated or manual rollback; 4) provide a dry-run simulation mode that estimates rollback surface and risk profile. This ticket covers the Terraform module surface (inputs/outputs), the plan/execution metadata format, health-check hooks, and the minimal operator shim to orchestrate plan validation, apply, and rollback decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes plan_mode (plan-only|apply|execute-with-attestations) and produces a signed plan artifact (plan_id, sha256, signer) saved to S3/remote state
Orchestration shim can validate a plan and run staged applies with configurable step timeouts and health probes
When a health gate fails, shim generates a rollback plan artifact and logs a suggested rollback PR (terraform state restore steps) to GitHub
Dry-run mode runs the upgrade simulator and returns a risk score and list of resources that would require rollback intervention
Module and shim emit structured telemetry (plan.started, step.completed, step.failed, rollback.generated) compatible with Console dashboards
End-to-end test exists in CI against a small private EKS fixture (cluster lifecycle test) that intentionally fails a step and verifies rollback plan creation
technical_notes: Design notes: - Use Terraform 1.6+ run_in_subprocess pattern to keep module idempotent and preserve state when execution is aborted. - Plan artifact (JSON) includes version, tfplan sha256, execution_id, signer metadata (Key ID), and an attestations array of per-step checks. - Health checks piggyback on existing probes: control-plane k8s readiness (apiserver SANs and cert rotation), kube-controller-manager health endpoints, and cloud-level checks (ENI attach, route table and SG validation). - The shim will call a small Lambda (or short-lived job) to run impermanent health probes from within the customer's VPC; results are returned as signed attestations to the plan. - Rollback planner is deterministic: uses plan artifact to reverse changes in reverse-step order with idempotent apply where possible (state restore + targeted terraform apply -target). - Telemetry uses existing tracing headers and sends events to Console with execution_id to tie logs, traces, and metrics. - Security: plan signer uses KMS ECDSA to avoid leaking secret material; signed artifacts stored with strict ACLs.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: A partially-applied control-plane change can make cluster unreachable and block future applies. Mitigation: stage changes in small steps; require explicit human approval for high-risk steps; provide a 'hold' window after each step for monitoring.
Risk: Signed plan artifacts become stale when external resources drift. Mitigation: include a plan TTL and preflight checks that re-run the key resource queries before allowing an apply.
Risk: Over-automation could trigger rollbacks during transient blips. Mitigation: health gates include short transient-tolerant windows and require multiple failed probes before rollback generation.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): prototype plan artifact schema and a minimal terraform module that emits plan metadata and writes to S3. Add unit tests for artifact generation.
Phase 2 (core, 2 sprints): implement orchestration shim that reads a signed plan, runs staged applies, and collects health attestations via VPC probes. Integrate telemetry events.
Phase 3 (hardening, 1 sprint): add deterministic rollback planner, add CI cluster test, and surface execution status in Console as a read-only Execution view.
Phase 4 (rollout): enable on a small set of internal private clusters behind a feature flag for 2 weeks; iterate on thresholds and timeouts.
